rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening fa makes this discussion connected to and derived from what precedes it.
rows.anchor: دلت الفاء على أن الكلام الواقع بعدها متصل بما قبلها ومتفرع عليه لا محالة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amma means whatever may happen; it strengthens the answer’s connection to the preceding discourse and introduces a contrast.
rows.anchor: ودلت ( أمّا ) على معنى : مهما يكن من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling earlier nations’ blessings, heedlessness, and punishment, the passage warns the Quraysh that their luxury and arrogance repeat that pattern.
rows.anchor: اشتمل على وصف ما كانت تتمتع به الأمم الممثّل بها مما أنعم الله عليها به من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists mistake prosperity for divine favor, reject the Messenger’s warning as inconsistent with their fortunes, and deny a contrasting afterlife.
rows.anchor: فحسبوا أن إنذار الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم إياهم بالعذاب ليس بصدق لأنه يخالف ما هو واقع لهم من النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their error rests on denying afterlife and resurrection and imagining worldly conditions endure; they confine reward to wealth and punishment to poverty.
rows.anchor: وقد تضمن هذا الوهَم أصولاً انبنى عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed fa derives this discussion from the general conclusion that God watches over all, explaining that His course follows knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: فاء التفريع مرتبطة بجملة : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbeliever supposes that abundance means God honored him, while restricted living means God humiliated him.
rows.anchor: فيتوهم خلاف ذلك إذ يحسب أن ما يناله من نعمة وسعة في الدنيا تكريما من الله له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating prosperity as proof of divine favor implies that God’s actions lack wisdom, a false inference also challenged by the cited verse.
rows.anchor: وهذا التوهم يستلزم ظنهم أفعال الله تعالى جارية على غير حكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning teaches believers not to let desire distort subtle evidence: worldly states vary and vanish, so they cannot establish a person’s standing with God.
rows.anchor: الأحوال الدنيوية أعراض زائلة ومتفاوتة الطول والقصر

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha says the Christian Ghassānids expected consequences and did not imagine that good could come without later evil or evil without lasting consequence.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة في آل غسان الذين لم يكونوا مشركين وكانوا متدينين بالنصرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poverty is named opposite blessing because the Meccan polytheists generally had healthy, strong bodies and died through killing or old age.
rows.anchor: لأن غالب أحوال المشركين المتحدث عنهم صحة المزاج وقوة الأبدان

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line about deadly places not sparing old age illustrates the stated pattern of death.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة : تَغْشَى مَتَالِفَ لا يُنْظِرْنَكَ الهَرَمَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says most commentators did not explain the verse’s arrangement and connection to its context, with al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya as exceptions.
rows.anchor: ولم يعرج أكثر المفسرين على بيان نظم الآية واتصالها بما قبلها عدا الزمخشري وابن عطية

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: Ṭarafa’s verse presents wealth and noble sons as a fortunate status that the speaker attributes to his Lord’s choice.
rows.anchor: قال طرفة : فلو شاءَ ربّي كنتُ قيسَ بنَ عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh, Tamīm, and Fazāra leaders asked Muhammad to dismiss poor believers, including ʿAmmār, Bilāl, Khabbāb, and Ṣuhayb, promising they might then follow; they made a similar request to Abū Ṭālib.
rows.anchor: لما أتى الملأ من قريش ومن بني تميم وفزارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly circumstances are no basis for judging recompense for deeds; the consistent recompense comes on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وأعلمهم أن أحوال الدنيا لا تتخذ أصلا في اعتبار الجزاء على العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān is a generic expression conventionally encompassing people, but intended here for polytheists who predominate in the audience.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس وتعريفه تعريف الجنس فيستغرق أفراد الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This generic usage for disbelievers resembles other Meccan passages and is reinforced by the later reference to the human remembering on that Day.
rows.anchor: { يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان وأنى له الذكرى }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for identifying the human as either ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa or Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: عتبة بن ربيعة أو أبو حذيفة بن الغيرة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī identify the human as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أمية بن خَلَف عن مقاتل والكلبي

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī also identifies the human as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أبيّ بن خلف عن الكلبي أيضاً

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the generic rebuke addresses a tendency prevalent among disbelievers, although some believers may also fall into it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : ومن حيث كان هذا غالبا على الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People mistake incidental benefits for God’s honor and harms for targeted vengeance, projecting desire and omens onto events without evidence.
rows.anchor: من ضلال أهل الشرك ومن فتنة الشيطان لبعض جهلة المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who call prosperity divine honor are not thereby worthy of God’s honor; those with restricted provision are not lower before Him than the prosperous.
rows.anchor: فهؤلاء الذين زعموا ما نالهم من نعمة الله إكراما من الله لهم ليسوا أهلا لكرامة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This error entrenches polytheism and diverts people from evidence; Ibn al-Rāwandī’s couplet depicts perplexity at the ignorant prospering while the learned suffer.
rows.anchor: عن تزلزل فهمهم وقلة علمهم بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge is vast and His varied actions follow wisdom; benefits and harms can arrive through several causes, familiar or extraordinary.
rows.anchor: وعلم الله واسع وتصرفاته شتى وكلها صادرة عن حكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly openings may precede sudden punishment when people forget admonition and rejoice in what they receive.
rows.anchor: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a warning, hardship may be replaced by ease; people wrongly regard both states as ordinary inherited fortune before sudden seizure.
rows.anchor: ثم بدلنا مكان السيئة الحسنة حتى عفوا وقالوا قد مس آباءنا الضراء والسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People can be tested repeatedly without repenting or remembering, so repeated events should not be read through wishful assumptions.
rows.anchor: أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some divine acts disclose what is intended for people, while others follow the ordained order of the world; the discerning take precautions and defer unclear matters to God.
rows.anchor: بعضها يدل على مراده من الناس وبعضها جار على ما قدره من نظام العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guided Muslims should avoid old pagan superstition, though heedless commoners may retain traces of it and should learn from this warning.
rows.anchor: وقد نجد في بعض العوامّ ومن يشبههم من الغافلين بقايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may hasten a good life as reward for a believing person who acts righteously.
rows.anchor: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may hasten punishment for those who incur His anger; Noah promised his people rain, wealth, and children if they sought forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فقلت استغفروا ربكم إنه كان غفارا يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ويمددكم بأموال وبنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also promises abundant water if people remain upright on the path.
rows.anchor: وألو استقاموا على الطريقة لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prominent sign of special divine treatment is that it occurs against the usual pattern, as in the Prophet’s and caliphs’ victories over mighty nations.
rows.anchor: أظهرها أن تجري على خلاف المألوف كما نرى في نصر النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amma usually introduces a paired contrast, not an unpacking of a prior summary; here it separates ease and abundance from hardship and restricted provision.
rows.anchor: فالمفصل هنا أحوال الإنسان الجاهل فصلت إلى حاله في الخفض والدعة وحاله في الضنك والشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author discussed amma’s use earlier in the commentary on al-Baqara 2:26.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم ذكر ( أمّا ) عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtalā means to test; both good and evil test steadfastness, forbearance, patience, and gratitude.
rows.anchor: والابتلاء : الاختبار ويكون بالخير وبالضرّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test can measure whether a person gives thanks or is ungrateful, as the cited verse says.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : { ليبلوني أأشكر أم أكفر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes either blessing or restricted provision a test of gratitude, disbelief, patience, or impatience, but the person mistakes it for honor or humiliation.
rows.anchor: إذا جعل ربه ما يناله من النعمة أو من التقتير مظهرا لحاله في الشكر والكفر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says ikrām may mean conveying an unblemished benefit or making someone or something noble in its kind.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : أن يُوصَل إلى الإِنسان كرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Rāghib’s distinction, God’s doing ikrām means granting benefit, while the person’s claim means being made noble or eminent.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { فأكرمه } من المعنى الأول للإِكرام

rows.speaker: المحققون من المتكلمين
rows.claim: The informed theologians, including al-Māturīdī and al-Bāqillānī, hold that unbelievers receive worldly blessings; the Ashʿarī–Māturīdī dispute is verbal.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه المحققون من المتكلمين أن الكافر مُنعَم عليه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naʿʿamahu means that God placed the person in blessing and comfortable living.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { نعّمه } جعله في نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaddara provision means giving it in a limited measure; taqtīr is another expression for scarcity, opposed to expanded provision.
rows.anchor: ومعنى : { فقدر عليه رزقه } أعطاه بقَدْر محدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in rizqahu may refer to the human, making provision the object of the verbal noun, or to the Lord, making Him its subject.
rows.anchor: والهاء في { رزقه } يجوز أن تعود إلى { الإنسان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihāna means treatment with lowliness and degradation.
rows.anchor: والإِهانة : المعاملة بالهون وهو الذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessing and restricted provision are attributed to God because His laws and causes arrange them, and events coincide with people at particular opportunities and times.
rows.anchor: لأن الكرامة والنعمة انساقت للإنسان أو انساق له قدر الرزق بأسباب من جعل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawl is literal speech, used because people voice their beliefs: they boast of blessing or complain of need while holding those beliefs.
rows.anchor: والقول مستعمل في حقيقته وهو التكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse likewise uses saying for believing a proposition and voicing it as a defense before one’s community.
rows.anchor: أي اعتقدوا ذلك فقالوه واعتذروا به لأنفسهم بين أهل ملتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing rabbī before the verbs strengthens the assertion and presents it as firm and unhesitating.
rows.anchor: وتقديم { ربي } على فعل { أكرمني } وفعللِ { أهانني }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sayings answer the two amma clauses and describe what the person says whenever either condition occurs.
rows.anchor: وجملتا : { فيقول } في الموضعين جوابان ل ( إمَّا ) الأولى والثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verbs convey recurrence and renewal of the claim whenever prosperity or restricted provision occurs.
rows.anchor: وأوثر الفعل المضارع في الجوابين لإفادة تكرر ذلك القول وتجدده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes both claims: worldly conditions do not prove a person’s standing with God; His intent is known through revelation rather than ordinary appearances.
rows.anchor: فهو ردع عن اعتقاد ذلك فمناط الردع كلا القولين لأن كل قول منهما صادر عن تأول باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited passage depicts people whose deeds and beliefs are misdirected although they think they are doing well.
rows.anchor: الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may be prosperous yet displeasing to God, while a disheveled, rejected poor person may be so favored that an oath on God’s behalf would be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: فرب رجل في نعمة في الدنيا هو مسخوط عليه ورب أشعث أغبر مطرود بالأبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects the inference that prosperity signals approval or poverty signals humiliation, not the fact that God bestows worldly benefits; disbelievers are humiliated in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وليس مناطه وقوع الكرامة ووقوع الإهانة لأن الله أهان الكافر بعذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If disbelief itself caused worldly humiliation through restricted provision, every unbeliever would be poor; thus poverty is not the sign being refuted.
rows.anchor: ولو شاء إهانته في الدنيا لأجل الكفر لأهان جميع الكفرة بتقتير الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction between God granting actual benefits and kallā, because kallā rejects the claim that those benefits prove divine approval.
rows.anchor: لأن الإبطال وارد على ما قصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s dealings have causes and purposes beyond ignorant conjecture; people should seek evidence through reason and revelation without forcing conclusions.
rows.anchor: أن لشأن الله في معاملته الناس في هذا العالم أسراراً وعللاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of knowledge place matters correctly and infer from guidance rather than confusing or misapplying evidence.
rows.anchor: وأما أهل العلم فهم يضعون الأشياء مواضعها

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers vocalize the final yāʾ in rabbī with fatḥa in both occurrences; the rest leave it quiescent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو { ربي } في الموضعين بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers read rabbī in both places with a quiescent final yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بسكونها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce qadara with a light dāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { فقدر عليه } بتخفيف الدال

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Jaʿfar pronounce qaddara with a doubled dāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وأبو جعفر بتشديد الدال

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ retains the yāʾ after each nūn in connected reading but drops it at pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع : { أكرمن } ، و{ أهانن } بياء بعد النون في الوصل وبحذفها في الوقف

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains the yāʾ in both connected reading and pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأهما ابن كثير بالياء في الوصل والوقف

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers omit the yāʾ in both connected reading and pause; the consonantal rasm lacks the yāʾ, without conflicting with transmitted readings.
rows.anchor: وقرأهما ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب بدون ياء في الوصل والوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal is a transitional shift, linked by contrast to the supposed honor of wealth: although they boast of divine favor, they fail to honor God’s servants.
rows.anchor: { بل } إضراب انتقالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They withhold surplus wealth from those in need while seeking more than they need, refuting their pride in generosity.
rows.anchor: إذ حرموا أهل الحاجة من فضول أموالهم وإذ يستزيدون من المال ما لا يحتاجون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orphan statement is a new sentence, either opening discourse or parenthetically separating the two kallā statements.
rows.anchor: فجملة : { لا تكرمون اليتيم } استئناف كما يقتضيه الإضراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honoring an orphan means meeting his needs and treating him kindly, since he has lost his provider and may be vulnerable around inherited property.
rows.anchor: وإكرام اليتيم : سد خلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatīm is a child whose father has died; the generic definite form means orphans collectively.
rows.anchor: { اليتيم } : الصبي الذي مات أبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the notion that prosperity or restricted provision results from God intending to honor or humiliate a person.
rows.anchor: { كلا } ردع عن هذا القول أي ليس ابتلاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This general rebuke is left unexplained because the conclusion about God watching over the earlier nations already summarizes their fate.
rows.anchor: وهذا ردع مجمل لم يتعرض القرآن لتبيينه اكتفاء بتذييل أحوال الأمم الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failing even to urge others to feed implies a fortiori that they themselves do not feed: they will not mediate, much less give.
rows.anchor: وهي دلالة فحوى الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿām may mean food itself, yielding an exhortation to give the poor person food, with the annexation marking entitlement.
rows.anchor: { طعام } يجوز أن يكون اسما بمعنى المطعوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ṭaʿām is the verbal noun of feeding, with the poor person as object: the rich are not urged to feed the poor.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون اسم مصدر أطعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miskīn means a poor person; its explanation was given earlier in Sūrat al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: و { المسكين } : الفقير وتقدم في سورة براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciprocal implication supplies omitted complements: not honoring orphans entails not urging their guardians to honor them; not urging food entails not feeding the poor from one’s wealth.
rows.anchor: وقد حصل في الآية احتباك لأنهم لما نفي إكرامهم اليتيم وقوبل بنفي أن يحضوا على طعام المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Urging others to feed can stand for feeding oneself, because someone who urges an act wants to do it and performs it when able.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الحض على الطعام كناية عن الإطعام لأن من يحض على فعل شيء يكون راغبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to urge truth and patience likewise means practicing them as well as encouraging them.
rows.anchor: أي عملوا بالحق وصبروا وتواصوا بهما

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers use second-person forms, shifting from the earlier third-person framing to confront the audience with a more forceful rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : « لا تكرمون ، ولا تحضون ، وتأكلون ، وتحبون » بالمثناة الفوقية على الخطاب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read the verbs in third person, informing the Prophet and believers of the audience’s conduct, as in the cited passage.
rows.anchor: وقرأها أبو عمرو ويعقوب بالمثناة التحتية على الغيبة لتعريف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمسلمين بذلك

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers vocalize taḥuḍḍūna with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ as the imperfect of ḥaḍḍa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { ولا تحضُّون } بضم الحاء مضارع حضّ

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وخلف
rows.claim: These readers use taḥāḍḍūna with fatḥa and an alif, reduced from tataḥāḍḍūna, meaning that people urge one another not to feed.
rows.anchor: وقرأه عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وخلف { تَحَاضُّون } بفتح الحاء وألف بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence may be spoken aloud in regret, functioning circumstantially with al-insān or as an inclusive substitute for the remembrance clause.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { يقول يا ليتني } الخ يجوز أن يكون قولا باللسان تحسرا وتندما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may be an inward statement explaining what the person remembers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قوله في نفسه فتكون الجملة بيانا لجملة { يتذكر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of qaddamtu is omitted for concision.
rows.anchor: ومفعول { قدمت } محذوف للإيجاز .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may mark time: the speaker wishes he had sent deeds ahead during his first life, before death.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله : { لحياتي } تحتمل معنى التوقيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām marks purpose: he wishes he had done righteous deeds for complete life free from punishment.
rows.anchor: وتحتمل أن يكون اللام للعلة ، أي قدمت الأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life in punishment is described as neither truly dying nor living, supporting the sense of full life free from torment.
rows.anchor: لأن حياتهم في العذاب حياة غشاوة وغياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative yā draws attention to the wish and underscores its importance on the day it occurs.
rows.anchor: وحرف النداء في قوله : { يا ليتني } للتنبيه اهتماما بهذا التمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After fully presenting warning and threat, the discourse ends with glad tidings for believers who remembered through the Qur’an and followed its guidance, matching the Qur’an’s alternation of warning and good news.
rows.anchor: لما استوعب ما اقتضاه المقام من الوعيد والتهديد والإنذار ختم الكلام بالبشارة للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This alternation increases people’s desire to do good and fear of evil.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك مما يزيد رغبة الناس في فعل الخير ورهبتهم من أفعال الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its placement after the preceding verses suggests it was revealed with them in one sequence, so this speech belongs to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: واتصال هذه الآية بالآيات التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may be spoken on Judgment Day as the answer to an omitted speech after the earth is crushed, with intervening material as an aside.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يقال يومَ الجزاء فهو مقول قولٍ محذوف هو جواب ( إذا )
